articles.title: ‘I haven’t thrown anyone under the bus’: Usman Khawaja defends timing of ball-tampering revelations
articles.summary: Former Test opener issues explanation on social media. Khawaja says he would ‘not deny’ everyone knew about sandpaper. Usman Khawaja insists he has not thrown anyone under the bus with his bombshell ball-tampering revelations that have rocked Australian cricket.
body: One day on from claiming sandpaper had been used in the Test prior to Cape Town 2018 and the entire team were responsible, Khawaja defended the timing of his claims.
In a five-minute long, two-part Instagram explanation, Khawaja revealed he had planned to go public with the details days after the incident before the suspended Steve Smith talked him out of it.
He also detailed how he made another attempt to ensure the entire team took the blame for it in 2021, before a public statement from the bowlers denied any knowledge.

But Khawaja said he had made a promise with his childhood friend David Warner to spill the details of the saga post-retirement in his book, believing Warner, Smith and Cameron Bancroft had taken the fall for the entire team.

articles.title: FA Cup roundup: Charlie Savage gets one over dad Robbie as Reading thrash Peterborough
articles.summary: Non-league Kidderminster stun Doncaster. Exeter upset Huddersfield in first round. Charlie Savage scored against his father’s team as Reading eased into the second round of the FA Cup with a 5-0 rout of Peterborough at the Weston Homes Stadium.
body: This all-League One tie turned out to be one of the most one-sided of the day, with the Peterborough manager, Robbie Savage, watching on in disbelief as his side were pulled apart.

Reading went ahead after 26 minutes as slick passing led to Andy Rinomhota playing in Daniel Kyerewaa, who found the bottom corner via a deflection. Reading doubled their lead in the 34th minute when a cross from Haydon Roberts was met by a diving header from top scorer Jack Marriott.
It was in effect game over in first-half stoppage time as Savage deepened his father’s misery when he took possession after the ball ran off Marriott, his deflected effort finding the top corner.

Jamie Reid added a fourth for the visitors in the 72nd minute when Paudie O’Connor nodded Savage’s free-kick into his path for him to lift over the Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass. Reading struck yet again four minutes later when Liam Fraser’s pass put Reid clean through to score his second.

articles.title: Billam-Smith stopped as Clarke repeats amateur win
articles.summary: Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith is knocked down and stopped for the first time in his professional career as Chev Clarke wins their non-title bout.
body: Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight on Saturday.
Londoner Clarke landed a big right hand at the start of the seventh round and although Billam-Smith beat the count, he was down again moments later after a barrage of punches.
The contest was allowed to continue but the Bournemouth fighter looked unsteady on his legs and when Clarke connected with two more blows, the referee stepped in.
Billam-Smith immediately protested against the decision, while Clarke stood in the middle of the ring shrugging his shoulders.

articles.summary: Valverde opens scoring in 3-0 victory for Real Madrid. Bayern beat Mainz but Neuer’s record-breaking day turns sour. Kylian Mbappé scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia on Saturday.
body: Reigning champions Barça visit Atlético Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. José Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla stadium as they secured an eighth win in a row across all competitions.

Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat and Mbappé added a third in the second half, bursting on to a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Stole Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign.

Bayern Munich secured a 2-1 victory over Mainz in the Bundesliga on Saturday but the form ⁠of goalkeeper Manuel Neuer will again be in the spotlight after another error almost produced an equaliser for the home side ⁠in the first ⁠half.

Neuer became Bayern’s ​oldest player at 40 years, 225 days, overtaking Bernd Dreher, but was forced off with a recurrence of a foot injury ⁠that had kept him out of recent matches, replaced before half-time by Jonas Urbig.

articles.summary: Rangers win 2-0 to go one point off top spot. Aberdeen slump to 4-0 defeat against Hibernian. Rangers banished their recent away day blues with a solid 2-0 win at St Mirren.
body: Draws against Dundee and Hearts in their last two Scottish Premiership games away from Ibrox had blemished their title challenge, but Derek McInnes’s side were determined to leave Paisley without a mark on them.

The in-form striker Ryan Naderi scored with a soft penalty after 18 minutes before the returning skipper, Dan Neil, added a second just after the hour mark with a deflected strike to extend Rangers’ unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 games.

Rangers moved to within one point of the leaders, Celtic, having played the same number of fixtures, albeit Celtic can restore their four-point lead if they beat Kilmarnock at home on Sunday before the international break gives them another breather.
The Aberdeen manager, Stephen Robinson, insists he will face the challenge head on as his side go into the international break in real trouble at the wrong end of the table.

articles.title: 'The worst conditions in my 35-year career' - commentating in the FA Cup fog
articles.summary: BBC Sport commentator Steve Bower gives an insight into trying to commentate when thick fog engulfs a stadium and you can barely see the action.
body: One of the most important attributes for a commentator is to be able to see the action you are trying to describe but that became a luxury for BBC Sport's Steve Bower when Altrincham hosted Notts County in an FA Cup tie on Saturday.
As thick fog enveloped the Moss Lane ground, he could barely see what was going on in a first-round game being televised live on BBC Two.
"One of the more challenging of my long career, that's about 35 years now," said Bower about the experience.
"I was reminded by a colleague - maybe I'm a jinx - that we had a similar thing on the BBC about three years ago when we did York against Wigan in the first round and the fog came in.

articles.title: 'Very disappointed' Russell says Mercedes error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole
articles.summary: George Russell said he was "really disappointed" as he insisted a "misjudgement" by his Mercedes team had cost him pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
body: Russell drove impressively throughout a hugely-challenging wet qualifying session at Interlagos but ultimately missed out on pole position by two tenths to McLaren's Lando Norris.
The Mercedes driver had led Norris by four tenths of a second after their first runs in Q3, but was then told to abort his second run when he was being held up by the Williams of Alex Albon.

Mercedes thought that Russell would have time to complete another push lap, but the rain intensified moments later and prevented anyone from going faster for the seven minutes of the session that remained.

Russell reacted with fury over team radio, questioning the instruction for him to abort and insisting that regardless of the time he was losing behind Albon, he would have been able to better Norris' time.

articles.title: 'We squashed it' - Hamilton reveals details of talks with Leclerc after fall out
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have "squashed" their incident at the Mexico City Grand Prix after holding talks in Brazil.
body: Hamilton, Leclerc and team principal Frederic Vasseur held talks on Thursday night to discuss the incident which saw Max Verstappen take advantage of the opening lap Ferrari squabble last Sunday to win the race.
Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future.
Hamilton will start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix due to a power unit change and spoke to the media for the first time on Saturday since his talks with Leclerc.
"Me and Charles sat and spoke and we squashed it, and we're moving on," he told Sky Sports F1.

articles.title: Notre Dame 4, Penn State 2: Five-Alarm Fire
articles.summary: Penn State hockey fell to 2-7-1 with a 4-2 loss to Notre Dame on Saturday night. The Nittany Lions scored the first goal but were completely flattened in the final 40 minutes of regulation in another embarrassing loss as we hit the 10-game mark of the season. First Period.
body: Penn State came out firing on all cylinders and put up more sustained zone time in the first period than they did at any point last night. Patrick Quinlan made several point-blank saves, including two with Shea Busch uncontested in front of the net.
Notre Dame pressured a bit, but the Nittany Lions took their 1-0 lead to the locker room and made way for the annual Teddy Bear Toss.

Just as they did last night, Notre Dame took control of the game in the second period. Carter Slaggert tied the game 39 seconds into the second, and the Fighting Irish immediately swung the momentum of the game. Penn State struggled to generate a consistent attack in the middle period, and the chippy play started to pick up throughout.

A commotion behind the net resulted in the puck finding a wide open Danny Nelson in front of the net. Nelson easily beat Josh Fleming to give Notre Dame a 2-1 lead. The ugly defensive play continued for Penn State throughout the second period, and Penn State was fortunate to escape the second only trailing by a goal.

articles.title: One daring shot was all La Salle needed to repeat as state soccer champs
articles.summary: PROVIDENCE – Camryn Bromage just couldn't help herself, and that turned out to be the best thing for La Salle on this Saturday afternoon at Rhode Island College. The junior midfielder had time to take a shot midway through the first half against Cumberland.
body: Bromage managed to find the net and make the difference at Alumni Stadium as the Rams sealed back-to-back Division I titles with a 1-0 win over the Clippers under gray skies on Nov. 7.
"My coach was like, 'Do not take that shot.' It was a little far out," Bromage said. "But I had the space, I had the opportunity and I just shot it."

Bromage took aim in the 15th minute after a tense start between a pair of familiar contenders. Her right-footed effort skipped at the top of the 6-yard box and found its way inside the right post, aided by turf still slick from the overnight rain. That moment allowed La Salle to flip what was its lone defeat of the season, a loss by the same score line against Cumberland at home.
"It's a wet game," Bromage said. "The field is slippery. It just so happened it went through."

“I don’t know what happened at the end of the game. I put my headset down, I called victory formation. All we had to do was just take a knee and nail the clock out. That’s just situational football. I don’t know what happened in regards to that. I looked up and we was running the ball, and then I seen the fumble. But my final instructions was victory formation. That’s when you kneel it out, and they had, I think, zero timeouts left, and the game was over practically.”
When a reporter asked him to clarify, Vick repeated that he called victory and said he doesn’t know why a run play was called.

“I put my headset down, and I took my headset off ’cause all we had to do was just run it three times, or two times, or kneel it out. I just called victory. I don’t know what happened. A run play was called. I looked up, I seen us running the ball. I don’t know what happened. I really don’t. I don’t know what the play call was. I don’t know why we even ran that play.”
